questions.stem: A distress alert was sent by accident. What must be done?
options: Cancel it immediately
Wait to see if anyone responds
Switch off the radio and say nothing
Wait for the end of the voyage
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 244 requires immediate cancellation under IMO A.814(19).

questions.stem: Which is the correct set of cancel steps for a VHF DSC false alert (RAMN)?
options: Switch to Channel 70 and wait for MCTS to call
Call the owner by phone and let them tell MCTS
Press the distress button again to cancel it
Switch off, go to Channel 16, and broadcast a cancellation
questions.explanation: The RAMN gives these steps, with the date and time stated in UTC.

questions.stem: In the cancel broadcast, how is the date and time of the original alert stated?
options: In local time only
In tide-table time
In UTC
No time is stated
questions.explanation: RAMN: 'cancel my distress alert of' followed by the date and time in UTC.

questions.stem: How long must the radio record be kept?
options: 12 months after the first entry
At least 12 months after the last entry
30 days after the end of the voyage, then destroyed
Until the next radio inspection

questions.stem: A paper radio record must be kept:
options: in its original format
recopied neatly each year
as a photograph only
in a safe ashore

questions.stem: Who initials entries in the radio record?
options: The master only
The Coast Guard officer
The owner, when the log is sent ashore each month
The radio operator making the entry

questions.stem: What must be recorded about an inadvertent distress transmission?
options: Nothing, if it was cancelled quickly
Only the vessel's position at the time
The time sent, and the time and method of cancelling
Only the MMSI and the channel used

questions.stem: How must a radio operator state the time on a domestic BC voyage in voice communications?
options: UTC only, in the 12-hour system
Local 24-hour time, four figures, with the zone
Tide-table time for the nearest port
Ship's clock time, with no zone given
questions.explanation: Section 246: UTC on an international voyage, local time otherwise; 24-hour, four figures, followed by the time zone identifier.

questions.stem: At sea, how often is a VHF installation assessed and tested?
options: Assessed daily; tested weekly by a call
Tested daily by sending a distress alert
Assessed and tested once a month
Tested only before each voyage

questions.stem: A radio has been out of service for 40 days. What must the operator do?
options: Nothing, as long as it powers up
Verify it after the voyage is over and log the result
Replace the antenna before sailing
Verify it within 7 days before the voyage and log it
questions.explanation: Section 237(5) applies when out of service for more than 30 days.

questions.stem: What does s. 245 say about transmitter power?
options: Always use full power to be heard
Use low power only at night
Except in distress, use no more power than needed
Power may not be adjusted by the operator

questions.stem: When must the radio equipment be confirmed to be in proper operating condition?
options: After the voyage, before it is logged
Before the vessel embarks on a voyage
Once a year at the radio inspection
Only after a fault has been reported
